findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda nozzle on the soda machine at the drive-thru was observed containing soil accumulations. PIC was made aware. PIC removed the nozzle and it was cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water sitting in the mop bucket by the utility sink. PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that the mop water may have been from the night before. The mop water was disposed appropriately. Ensure that dirty water from mopping is disposed immediately after mopping at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed.
1. The caulking on the hand sink by the office was observed loose and not sealed to the wall. 
2. An accumulation of ice buildup was observed behind the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer. 
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the hand sink will be caulked and the ice accumulation cleaned. Ensure that the caulking onto hand sink is re-done and the accumulated Ice cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several utensils in storage were observed with remaining food debris on them. The PIC confirmed that the storage location should be clean items and moved the entire container back to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage in the facility. It is highly suggested that the employees that conduct dish washing procedures be re-educated to ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage moving forward.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be ice build-up in the standalone freezer, as well as the WIF. Ice seems to be emanating from the cooling element in both cases. Discussed with PIC, PIC informed inspector that standalone freezer had just been serviced. Ensure that it is serviced again, along with the walk-in freezer to prevent the build-up of ice in the freezers.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed there to be a gap between the cove base on the mop sink, and the mop sink basin. This gap needs to be filled to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. Discussed with PIC. Ensure this area is caulked, or the gap is otherwise filled to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface transition.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels were available at the hand sink by the kitchen entrance. COS.  Ensure paper towels are available at the hand sinks at all times.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon inspector arrival, there were papers and used disposable gloves in the hand sink.  Items were removed, COS.  Ensure the hand sinks are only used for hand washing.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
No sanitizer buckets were made at time of inspection.  Discussed with PIC, COS.  Ensure sanitizer buckets are made and available during all hours of operation to properly sanitize food contact surfaces.

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas needed to be sealed or caulked to create a smooth, non-absorbent, easily cleanable surface:
-Top of 3 part sink where it adjoins to the wall
-Hand sink by the main kitchen entrance door
-Hand sink by the soda machine

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of cleaning that contain dust/food debris:
-The ceiling vents over the prep coolers
-The floor/wall under the drive thru computer
Ensure these areas are cleaned regularly to prevent pest/rodent attraction and food contamination.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Aprons used for dish washing were observed to be hung on the side of the self containing clean dishes.  Discussed with PIC, who removed the aprons.  Ensure soiled aprons are stored in a place away from food and food contact surfaces.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon inspector arrival, the hand sink by the dish area contained a paper towel and spatula.  An employee removed the items.  Ensure the hand washing sinks are only use for hand washing.  If items waiting to be washed fall in the sink, ensure they are removed immediately.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The walk-in freezer is leaking water by the fan, and therefore creating large icicles hanging down from the vent area.  The PIC stated a call has been made to a company to fix it, but has not come to look at it yet.  The employees are presently knocking and chipping away the ice that forms every couple of days.  Ensure the freezer is serviced in a timely matter as to not cause any future damage to the unit.

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Non-food contact surfaces observed to contain an accumulation of dust:
-The grate of the fan in the walk-in cooler
-The fan on the food line
-The fan in the dish area
Ensure these items are cleaned regularly to prevent food contamination.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

In walk-in units (both refrigerator and freezer) There is dust accumulation observed. In the walk-in freezer, there is small dust accumulation on the fans on the condenser. In the refrigerator there is dust accumulation on piping behind condenser as well as dust accumulation on the line containing wiring for lightbulb in unit. At this time, no contamination risk exists due to all foods being properly sealed and/or unopened in boxes. See that these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 

In area containing soda lines in back of restaurant near water heater closet- a piece of nudo board is coming off the wall, creating a considerable gap for moisture and/or pests to get inside. See that this portion of wall is repaired so wall covering is flush with wall and gap is sealed. Will follow up at next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Observed some ice build up in the walk-in freezer both behind the condenser and around the door frame, making it difficult to close the door properly. See that the walk-in freezer is free of ice accumulation by next routine inspection. Note: this violation does not affect cold holding temperatures of TCS foods as the walk-in freezer is located within the walk-in cooler.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed dust and debris buildup in the hood crevices above the fryers. Service sticker indicates hood cleaning was due 10-26-20 by Lindsey's II Pro Hood Cleaning. Contact hood cleaning company and schedule a routine cleaning. Will check at next routine inspection.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed scoops for shredded cheese in the prep line with handles in contact with food. Ensure all handles are kept out of food to prevent contamination. PIC removed the handles from the cheese.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans in walk-in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed dust accumulation on fans in walk-in cooler. Ensure debris is cleaned off fans routinely to prevent from being blown onto food in the cooler. Will check next routine inspection. Discussed with person in charge.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the handsink by the dish area. Paper towels were provided during the inspection.

Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in sani-bucket by the front make line handsink was less than 100ppm. Solution was discarded and new solution prepared at proper concentration of 100ppm. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 100ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 (E)(4) Lower left edge of the drive thru soda machine ice shoot had mold accumulation. Ice shoot was sanitized during the inspection. 
Lobby soda machine was observed with heavy mold accumulation where nozzles attach to the machine. Manager sanitized the area in question during the inspection. 

Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and ice shoots of soda machines shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 - Employee did not change gloves after handling boxes of recently delivered dry goods and prior to returning to the make line. Employee washed hands and changed gloves at the request of the manager. 

Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 - Low lying area under the make line where a floor drain was previously located was observed with ponding water and debris accumulation. A slight odor was present as well. Management was advised to clean under the make line and get the area repaired to eliminate ponding water. 

Men's room handsink and inside the toilet were soiled with general buildup. Clean in the restrooms daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367, Section 3.07 Certified food manager on duty did not have food allergen awareness training completed. Requirements for allergen training were discussed. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed a container of white powder with no label. Provide a label on all unmistakable powders.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 1). Observed the tray underneath the prep line soiled with food debris. 2). Observed the bottom prep line cooler near the drive-thru area to be soiled with food debris. 3). Observed the cinnamon container top to have food debris. 4). Observed the shelves near the handsink of the right side of the facility to have dust accumulation. 5). Observed the bottom warmer door to have food splash. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the outside dumpster lid to be open. Close the outside dumpster lid to prevent rodents and waste water.
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1). REPEAT: Observed the floor in the walk-in cooler to be soiled with food debris. 2). Observed the floor underneath the single service storage shelves to be soiled.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Observed the hand sink near the vacant unit needs recaulking. Recaulk the hand sink near the vacant unit.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Three scoops were stored on top of three bulk food containers.  The top of the containers were soiled.  CORRECTED - managers immediately placed all three scoops and all three lids into dish area to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.  If scoops are not stored within food, then they must be stored clean and dry, in a way that protects them from contamination.

750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces are soiled:
(a) cabinet door, and cabinet itself, under drive-thru hand sink (syrup) (REPEAT), 
(b) rim around door frame of lower coolers on both sides of prep island (black mold), 
(c) surfaces/ledges/condenser coils under side breakfast prep station, 
(d) inside breakfast top-loading prep cooler (water, food debris), 
(e) floor fan (in front of drive-thru hand sink) ,
(f) condenser/fans in walk-in freezer.
Clean and maintain these surfaces.  Consider increasing frequency with which breakfast top-loading prep cooler is cleaned.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

The following floors are soiled:
(a) walk-in freezer, 
(b) under breakfast prep station area, 
(c) under drive-thru area shelves/counters.
Clean and maintain these floors.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:

CORRECTED - mop was immediately hung to dry and mop bucket was completely emptied.  Make sure mop buckets are emptied entirely to eliminate standing water for pests.

750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.

Clean all floors of accumulation of food debris and grease.

findings.comment:

750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non-food contact surfaces are soiled:  (A) inside lower cabinets under several hand sinks, (B) pipes & table legs of three-pan sink (IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED), (C) around black drop box on lower shelf of stainless steel prep table near three-pan sink, (D) wheels of equipment in fryer area, (E) door of lower cabinet under drive-thru hand sink (cherry syrup) (REPEAT), ...continued in General Comments.                          750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
[1] Both Drive-Thru Windows have gaps along the bottom (with some gaps along vertical line).  Seal these windows to be tight-fitting, so no daylight shines through.  [2] East outer doors have gaps along bottom.  While South door has a tighter-fitting door jam, it too has gaps along bottom.  Seal all doors and windows so no daylight is observed shining through.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

750-1220 Clean the floors.                750-1200 All floors must be in good repair.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: [1] Ceiling vents by walk-in cooler have dust accumulation.  Manager states they are cleaned at the end of each month.  Given the amount of dust accumulation, facility may consider increasing the frequency with which the vents are cleaned.  Clean dust accumulation found today.  [2] The following walls/ceilings/attached equipment are in disrepair:  (A) caulking at back of three-pan sink, (B) ceiling tile near hot water heater closet (ajar from recent repairs), (C) lobby mop sink (caulking moldy, in disrepair).  Repair/replace all caulking and replace ceiling tile.  ....continued in General Comments                                   750-1220 Clean the walls and ceilings.  750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair.
